task.name: A failed story's artifacts contain no primary evidence of why it failed, only the agent's account of itself
task.story_text:
## Observed

Observed in sprint issues-248,245,246,231, story #248, which forge reported as
"Dev attempt produced no usable output (no commits)" after a single dev attempt.

The only account anywhere in the run artifacts of why no commit was produced is the
dev agent's own closing prose, which claimed it could not write the story worktree's
git index lock. No captured command output, exit status, or error text supports or
contradicts that claim.

The run's audit record has an empty dev loop, empty gate decisions, empty gate debug,
and empty gate diagnostics. Its sandbox capabilities block exists but is unpopulated.
The agents directory under the run root is empty. No raw agent standard output or
standard error is retained anywhere for the story. The audit substrate entry for the
run contains nothing about the failure mechanism beyond the same summary sentence.

The failure is consequently unattributable. Three sibling stories in the same sprint
ran with identical recorded capabilities against identically structured worktrees;
one of them made six commits from the same layout, and another reported the same
environment restrictions and committed anyway. Every structural explanation available
from the artifacts — recorded capabilities, worktree git plumbing, repository hooks —
is identical between the story that failed and the ones that did not. The operator
cannot determine what was different, and neither can forge.

## Expected

When a story fails, its retained artifacts should carry enough primary
evidence to establish the cause independently of what the agent said about itself.
An agent's description of its own environment is a claim to be corroborated, not a
record of what happened; when it is the only thing kept, a failure becomes
permanently undiagnosable and any classification built on it is unfalsifiable. The
evidence that a run's own tooling captured should be sufficient to distinguish a
failure from a sibling run that succeeded under the same recorded conditions.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** a story that fails abnormally leaves no audit record, so
  the only account of the failure is the agent's own prose or a log line — and in
  several cases that account is destroyed before it is read.

- **Evidence:** four independent recurrences since this issue was filed, all in
  this repository.

  Sprint `65170a26ae8a` (2026-07-29) dropped `issue-2048` and `issue-2060` at
  launch with `cost_usd: 0.0`. Audit records exist for the three stories that
  landed and for neither of the two that failed. Both had in fact produced
  commits — five between them, later recovered from the branches.

  Sprint `7272950c8b34` (2026-08-01) lost `issue-2054` to a worker exception
  (`FileNotFoundError` on the advisory artifact, filed as #2107). No audit record
  was written. The exception text existed only in `.forge/sprints/*/state.yaml`,
  and the subsequent resume **overwrote that file**, so the record the issue was
  filed from no longer exists on disk.

  `forge status` unlinks each agent sidecar as it reaps it
  (`process_group.py:413`), so `.forge/runs/agents/` was empty immediately after
  each of the three occasions the orphan reaper was investigated (#2115). The
  records that would explain how those sidecars came to be written are destroyed
  by the same command that reports them.

  Plan review of `issue-2050` retained only the final attempt per reviewer; the
  first response survived as a truncated log preview and nowhere else (#2066,
  since fixed).

- **Confirmed cause:** the audit record is finalized at the end of a run. A story
  that is dropped before dispatch, or terminated mid-run by an exception, never
  reaches finalization, so the runs with the least recoverable context are
  precisely the ones that produce no record. Where a fallback artifact does hold
  the cause, nothing protects it from being overwritten by a later attempt at the
  same story.

- **Affected code path:** audit finalization in
  `src/theforge/coordinator/audit.py`; the sprint worker's exception path; the
  launch-guard drop path in `src/theforge/sprint/launch_guard.py`; sprint state
  rewriting on resume.

- **Fix-success criterion:** a story that terminates abnormally — dropped at
  launch, killed by an exception, or timed out — leaves an audit record naming the
  primary cause, and a later attempt at the same story does not overwrite the
  recorded cause of an earlier one.

handoff.summary: Extended the abnormal-termination audit path so every exit that never returns a CoordinatorResult leaves primary evidence. Added a stdlib-only sprint/abnormal.py holding the kind vocabulary (launch_guard_drop, worker_exception, worker_timeout, shared_infrastructure_failure), a cause builder, and an attempt-scoped history merge. Factored the timeout and worker-exception result construction into _abnormal_story_result, which also synthesizes a run id so a story that never reached the engine is still addressable as a run, and used it for launch-guard drops (stamped Phase.INIT, never overwriting the audit.yaml of the generation that actually ran). The cause is carried on CoordinatorState.abnormal_termination and emitted by generate_audit_log, with the per-run record schema bumped 17->18 plus a reader-side migration and regenerated snapshot fixture. Made retained failure evidence attempt-scoped: StoryStateEntry gained an append-only failure_history, and both writers of .forge/sprints/<id>/state.yaml (the runner's incremental persist and the end-of-sprint summary write) merge histories instead of replacing them, with prior history read unconditionally rather than only on resume.

Pinned by test_launch_guard_drop_writes_a_run_audit_naming_the_reason and test_stranded_worktree_drop_also_leaves_a_record. Reconciled-prior-DONE and preserved-escalated drops deliberately do not get a synthetic record: they are not failures and already have the real run's audit.

Pinned by test_worker_exception_audit_names_the_exception. The shared-infrastructure branch gets a distinct kind so the substrate/story attribution split from #2107 is preserved.

acceptance_criteria.notes: Existing timeout record retained and now carries kind=worker_timeout; pinned by test_worker_timeout_audit_names_the_timeout.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A later attempt at the same story does not overwrite the recorded cause of an earlier one.
acceptance_criteria.notes: accumulate_failure_history is applied at both writers of the sprint's accumulated state and at the live story-state entry. Prior history is loaded from disk unconditionally, because a plain re-run (not only a --resume) rewrites that file. Pinned by test_second_generation_does_not_erase_the_first_generations_cause (seam, two run_sprint generations) plus unit tests for merge, idempotency, and success-entry exclusion.

17 pre-existing test failures persist in this sandbox (POSIX semaphore and mkstemp permission denials in test_sprint_lock.py, test_sprint_reexec_collision.py, test_cut_rc_isolation.py). Identical set before and after this change; unrelated to it.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the P1. The per-run audit already named the cause for worker exceptions and timeouts, but the sprint's accumulated story row lost it: those rows spell their outcome with the coordinator Phase name (ESCALATE) while abnormal._FAILED_OUTCOMES only listed the StoryOutcome name (ESCALATED), so derive_failure_cause skipped exactly those rows and a later generation replaced them with no cause. Fixed at both ends — the retention set now recognises both spellings, and the cause no longer has to be re-derived from prose at all: a new carry_failure_cause helper stamps state.abnormal_termination (kind, run id, observing code path) onto the row, and all three story-row writers use it (runner._persist_current_story_result, runner._record_current_story_entry, and the results branch of audit._write_sprint_summary, the line the finding cited). Merging is deduped by (run_id, kind, cause) so several writers touching one row in one generation record one attempt. Prior iteration's work is unchanged: launch-guard drops, worker exceptions (both the future-collection and in-worker handlers), timeouts, and shared-infrastructure failures each synthesize a CoordinatorResult with a run id and an abnormal_termination block; generate_audit_log emits it; per-run record schema is v18 with a reader-side migration.

finding_registry.description: After a story ends with a worker exception or timeout, the final accumulated sprint state row contains no failure_history, and a later successful generation replaces that row with no retained cause from the failed attempt.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
